extracted.intended_audience: FCC-regulated entities (broadcast licensees/permittees, common carriers, cable operators, manufacturers, service providers), applicants, and counsel interacting with FCC enforcement and licensing procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural rules in 47 CFR Part 1 governing when applications are pending, reporting obligations, license modification and suspension, and assessment/assessment procedures and amounts for forfeitures (including tables of base amounts, service-specific amounts, adjustment criteria, time limits, notices, payment, and mitigation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'pending' application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is 'pending' before the Commission from the time it is accepted for filing by the Commission until a Commission grant or denial of the application is no longer subject to reconsideration by the Commission or to review by any court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications in broadcast services subject to competitive bidding - modification provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications in broadcast services subject to competitive bidding will be subject to the provisions of §§ 1.2105(b), 73.5002 and 73.3522 of this chapter regarding the modification of their applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to specific competitive bidding/modification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting of adverse findings by broadcast permittees and licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: All broadcast permittees and licensees must report annually to the Commission any adverse finding or adverse final action taken by any court or administrative body that involves conduct bearing on the permittee's or licensee's character qualifications and that would be reportable in connection with an application for renewal as reflected in the renewal form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File on the anniversary of the date the licensee's renewal application is required to be filed; licensees with multiple stations with different anniversary dates need file only one report per year on anniversary of their choice provided reports are not more than one year apart; permittees/licensees must make diligent, good faith efforts to become knowledgeable of such reportable adjudicated misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'adverse finding' and 'adverse final action' for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms 'adverse finding' and 'adverse final action' include adjudications made by an ultimate trier of fact, whether a government agency or court, but do not include factual determinations which are subject to review de novo unless the time for taking such review has expired under the relevant procedural rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pendency of an appeal does not relieve a permittee or licensee from its obligation to report the finding or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to cover construction permit — grant without hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for license by the lawful holder of a construction permit will be granted without hearing where the Commission, upon examination of such application, finds that all the terms, conditions, and obligations set forth in the application and permit have been fully met, and that no cause or circumstance arising or first coming to the knowledge of the Commission since the granting of the permit would, in the judgment of the Commission, make the operation of such station against the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to cover construction permit — designation for hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission is unable to make the findings required for grant without hearing, the Commission will designate the application for hearing upon specified issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds — willful or repeated failure to comply with license/authorization terms
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture penalty may be assessed against any person found to have willfully or repeatedly failed to comply substantially with the terms and conditions of any license, permit, certificate, or other instrument of authorization issued by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds — willful or repeated failure to comply with the Communications Act or Commission rules/orders
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture penalty may be assessed for willfully or repeatedly failing to comply with any of the provisions of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended; or of any rule, regulation or order issued by the Commission under that Act or under any treaty, convention, or other agreement to which the United States is a party and which is binding on the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds — violation of section 317(c) or 508(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture may be assessed for violation of any provision of section 317(c) or 508(a) of the Communications Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds — violation of sections 227(b) or 227(e) or related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture may be assessed for violation of any provision of sections 227(b) or (e) of the Communications Act or of §§ 64.1200(a)(1) through (5) and 64.1604 of this title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds — violation of section 511(a) or (b) or paragraph (b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture may be assessed for violation of any provision of section 511(a) or (b) of the Communications Act or of paragraph (b)(6) of § 1.80.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds — violation of certain Title 18 provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture may be assessed for violation of section 1304, 1343, or 1464 of Title 18, United States Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds — violation of section 6507 of the Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act of 2012 or Commission rules thereunder
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture may be assessed for violation of section 6507 of the Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act of 2012 or any rule, regulation, or order issued by the Commission under that statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds — violation of section 60506 of the Infrastructure and Jobs Act or 47 CFR part 16
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture may be assessed for violation of section 60506 of the Infrastructure and Jobs Act of 2021 or 47 CFR part 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of forfeiture penalties with other penalties (Note 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A forfeiture penalty assessed under this section is in addition to any other penalty provided for by the Communications Act, except that the penalties provided for in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4) shall not apply to conduct which is subject to a forfeiture penalty or fine under certain listed sections of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other provisions of the section remain applicable to such conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum forfeiture — broadcast station licensee, permittee, cable operator, or applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the violator is a broadcast station licensee or permittee, a cable television operator, or an applicant for any broadcast or cable television operator license, permit, certificate, or other instrument of authorization issued by the Commission, the forfeiture penalty shall not exceed $62,829 for each violation or each day of a continuing violation, except that the amount assessed for any continuing violation shall not exceed a total of $628,305 for any single act or failure to act described in paragraph (a) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No limit on forfeiture assessments for EEO violations by cable operators that occur after notification by the Commission of a potential violation. Higher ceilings for obscene/indecent/profane broadcasts (see next entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum forfeiture — obscene/indecent/profane broadcast by broadcast licensee/permittee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the violator (broadcast station licensee or permittee or applicant) is determined by the Commission to have broadcast obscene, indecent, or profane material, the forfeiture penalty shall not exceed $508,373 for each violation or each day of a continuing violation, except that the amount assessed for any continuing violation shall not exceed a total of $4,692,668 for any single act or failure to act described in paragraph (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum forfeiture — common carrier or applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the violator is a common carrier subject to the Communications Act or an applicant for any common carrier authorization, the forfeiture penalty shall not exceed $251,322 for each violation or each day of a continuing violation, except that the amount assessed for any continuing violation shall not exceed a total of $2,513,215 for any single act or failure to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum forfeiture — manufacturer or service provider under sections 255, 617, or 619
rubrics_metrics.description: If the violator is a manufacturer or service provider subject to the requirements of section 255, 716, or 718 of the Communications Act and is determined to have violated any such requirement, the manufacturer or service provider shall be liable for a forfeiture penalty of not more than $144,329 for each violation or each day of a continuing violation, except that the amount assessed for any continuing violation shall not exceed a total of $1,443,275 for any single act or failure to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum forfeiture — section 227(e) violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person determined to have violated section 227(e) of the Communications Act or the rules issued under that section shall be liable for a forfeiture penalty of not more than $14,432 for each violation or three times that amount for each day of a continuing violation, except that the amount assessed for any continuing violation shall not exceed a total of $1,443,275 for any single act or failure to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such penalty is in addition to any other forfeiture penalty provided for by the Communications Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture — section 227(b)(4)(B) violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person determined to have violated section 227(b)(4)(B) or rules in 47 CFR part 64 shall be liable for a forfeiture penalty determined in accordance with paragraphs (A)-(F) of section 503(b)(2) plus an additional penalty not to exceed $12,266.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture — pirate radio broadcasting
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Any person who willfully and knowingly does or causes or suffers to be done any pirate radio broadcasting shall be subject to a fine of not more than $2,453,218; and (ii) any person who willfully and knowingly violates the Act or any rule, regulation, etc., relating to pirate radio broadcasting shall, in addition, be subject to a fine of not more than $122,661 for each day during which such offense occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture — section 6507(b)(4) Tax Relief Act violation (unauthorized disclosure from Do-Not-Call registry)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a violator who is granted access to the Do-Not-Call registry of public safety answering points discloses or disseminates any registered telephone number without authorization, the monetary penalty shall be not less than $135,161 per incident nor more than $1,351,606 per incident depending upon whether the conduct was negligent, grossly negligent, reckless, or willful, and whether it was a first or subsequent offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture — section 6507(b)(5) Tax Relief Act violation (automatic dialing to Do-Not-Call registry number)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a violator uses automatic dialing equipment to contact a telephone number on the Do-Not-Call registry of public safety answering points, the monetary penalty shall be not less than $13,516 per call nor more than $135,161 per call depending on culpability and whether the violation was a first or subsequent offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture — failure to block illegal robocalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person determined to have failed to block illegal robocalls pursuant to §§ 64.6305(g) and 64.1200(n) shall be liable for a forfeiture penalty of no more than $25,132 for each violation, to be assessed on a per-call basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum forfeiture for cases not previously covered
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case not covered in paragraphs (b)(1) through (9), the amount of any forfeiture penalty shall not exceed $25,132 for each violation or each day of a continuing violation, except that the amount assessed for any continuing violation shall not exceed a total of $188,491 for any single act or failure to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in determining forfeiture amount
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the amount of the forfeiture penalty, the Commission or its designee will take into account the nature, circumstances, extent and gravity of the violations and, with respect to the violator, the degree of culpability, any history of prior offenses, ability to pay, and such other matters as justice may require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 2 service-unique forfeitures — broadcast-specific items

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 3 — Upward adjustment criteria for forfeitures
rubrics_metrics.description: Upward Adjustment Criteria: (1) Egregious misconduct; (2) Ability to pay/relative disincentive; (3) Intentional violation; (4) Substantial harm; (5) Prior violations of any FCC requirements; (6) Substantial economic gain; (7) Repeated or continuous violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors may be used to increase the base forfeiture amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 3 — Downward adjustment criteria for forfeitures
rubrics_metrics.description: Downward Adjustment Criteria: (1) Minor violation; (2) Good faith or voluntary disclosure; (3) History of overall compliance; (4) Inability to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors may be used to reduce the base forfeiture amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Section 503 forfeitures and application of downward adjustment factors (Table 4 note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other sections of the Act state prescribed amounts of forfeitures for violations; these amounts are subject to mitigation or remission under section 504. The Commission will apply the downward adjustment factors shown for section 503 forfeitures to these non-section 503 forfeitures where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 4 lists statutory amounts after inflation adjustment; amounts in table 4 are adjusted for inflation pursuant to DCIA; non-section 503 forfeitures may be adjusted downward using Table 3 downward adjustment criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation adjustments to maximum forfeiture amounts and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act Improvements Act of 2015, the statutory maximum amount of a forfeiture penalty assessed under this section shall be adjusted annually for inflation by order published no later than January 15 each year. Annual adjustments will be based on the CPI-U for October preceding the date of adjustment and OMB guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 5 provides the adjusted statutory maximum forfeitures after annual inflation adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits on initiating forfeiture proceedings — broadcast stations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a broadcast station, no forfeiture penalty shall be imposed if the violation occurred more than 1 year prior to issuance of the appropriate notice or prior to the date of commencement of the current license term, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date of commencement of the current license term means the date of commencement of the last term of license granted by the Commission; continuing licenses under section 307(c) pending decision on renewal do not create a new license term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits on initiating forfeiture proceedings — certain common carrier sections
rubrics_metrics.description: For forfeitures imposed against a carrier under sections 202(c), 203(e), and 220(d), no forfeiture will be imposed if the violation occurred more than 5 years prior to issuance of a notice of apparent liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits on initiating forfeiture proceedings — section 227(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a forfeiture imposed under section 227(e), none shall be imposed if the violation occurred more than 4 years prior to the date on which the appropriate notice was issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits on initiating forfeiture proceedings — section 227(b)(4)(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a forfeiture imposed under section 227(b)(4)(B), none shall be imposed if the violation occurred more than 4 years prior to the date on which the appropriate notice is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits on initiating forfeiture proceedings — other cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In all other cases, no penalty shall be imposed if the violation occurred more than 1 year prior to the date on which the appropriate notice is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary procedure before forfeiture for non-licensees/non-applicants (citation requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for certain specified forfeitures, no forfeiture shall be imposed on any person who does not hold a license/permit/authorization and is not an applicant unless, prior to issuance of the appropriate notice, such person: (1) is sent a citation reciting the violation charged; (2) is given a reasonable opportunity (usually 30 days) to request a personal interview with a Commission official at the nearest field office; and (3) subsequently engages in conduct of the type described in the citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A forfeiture may be imposed, however, if the person is engaged in activities for which authorization is required or in certain cable or tower-owner circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation procedure does not limit citations issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (c) does not limit the issuance of citations. When requirements satisfied for a particular violation by a particular person, a forfeiture may be imposed for conduct of that type without issuance of an additional citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIRATE Act preliminary procedure — skip notice of unlicensed operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent good cause, in any case alleging a violation of subsection (a) or (b) of section 511 of the Act, the Commission shall proceed directly to issue a notice of apparent liability for forfeiture without first issuing a notice of unlicensed operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative initiation procedures for forfeiture proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In the discretion of the Commission, a forfeiture proceeding may be initiated either by issuing a notice of apparent liability or a notice of opportunity for hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of apparent liability — content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of apparent liability will: (i) identify each specific provision, term, or condition which the respondent has apparently violated; (ii) set forth the nature of the act or omission charged and the facts upon which such charge is based; (iii) state the date(s) on which such conduct occurred; and (iv) specify the amount of the apparent forfeiture penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of apparent liability — delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of apparent liability will be sent to the respondent, by certified mail, at his last known address (see § 1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of apparent liability — response opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent will be afforded a reasonable period of time (usually 30 days from the date of the notice) to show, in writing, why a forfeiture penalty should not be imposed or should be reduced, or to pay the forfeiture. Any showing shall include a detailed factual statement and such documentation and affidavits as may be pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture order after notice of apparent liability
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed forfeiture penalty is not paid in full in response to the notice of apparent liability, the Commission, upon considering all relevant information available to it, will issue an order canceling or reducing the proposed forfeiture or requiring that it be paid in full and stating the date by which the forfeiture must be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial enforcement of forfeiture order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the forfeiture is not paid, the case will be referred to the Department of Justice for collection under section 504(a) of the Communications Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of opportunity for hearing — formal hearing procedures and review
rubrics_metrics.description: When a formal hearing under section 503(b)(3)(A) is held to determine whether to assess a forfeiture, the Commission may issue a notice of opportunity for hearing. The hearing shall be conducted by an administrative law judge under procedures in subpart B, including appeal and review. A final Commission order assessing a forfeiture under this paragraph is subject to judicial review under section 402(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to DOJ after forfeiture in hearing context
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after a forfeiture is imposed and not appealed or after a court enters final judgment in favor of the Commission, the forfeiture is not paid, the Commission will refer the matter to the Department of Justice for collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In an action to recover the forfeiture, the validity and appropriateness of the order imposing the forfeiture are not subject to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture issue in hearing where application dismissed — Commission may proceed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible assessment of a forfeiture is an issue in a hearing to determine whether a pending application should be granted, and the application is dismissed without a forfeiture determination by the presiding judge, the presiding judge shall forward the order of dismissal to the full Commission, which may proceed with a determination of whether a forfeiture is warranted and will provide the applicant a reasonable opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment method for forfeitures
rubrics_metrics.description: The forfeiture should be paid electronically using the Commission's electronic payment system in accordance with procedures on the Commission's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: URL provided: www.fcc.gov/licensing-databases/fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remission and mitigation of forfeitures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission, or its designee, may remit or reduce any forfeiture imposed under this section. After issuance of a forfeiture order, any request that it do so shall be submitted as a petition for reconsideration pursuant to § 1.106.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of amendments to paragraph (b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to paragraph (b) of this section implementing Pub. L. No. 101-239 are effective December 19, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial note on Federal Register citations affecting § 1.80 in Finding Aids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing procedures for amateur and commercial radio operator licenses (cross-reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application filing procedures for amateur radio operator licenses are set forth in part 97; application filing procedures for commercial radio operator licenses are set forth in part 13 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed info about commercial radio operator forms and filing procedures is available in the bulletin 'Commercial Radio Operator Licenses and Permits.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of operator licenses — notice and hearing opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever grounds exist for suspension of an operator license (per section 303(m)), the Chief of the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau may issue an order suspending the operator license; no order of suspension shall take effect until 15 days' notice in writing of the cause has been given to the operator licensee, who may make written application to the Commission at any time within the said 15 days for a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice is not effective until actually received; upon receipt of an application for hearing the suspension is designated for hearing and held in abeyance until conclusion of the hearing. If suspended, the operator must send the operator license to the Mobility Division by the effective date (or forthwith if effective date has passed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for emailing hearing application if conditions prevent immediate email
rubrics_metrics.description: If conditions prevent emailing of the application before the expiration of the 15-day period, the application shall then be emailed as soon as possible thereafter, accompanied by a satisfactory explanation of the delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of license or construction permit — notification and protest period
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever it appears that a station license or construction permit should be modified, the Commission shall notify the licensee or permittee in writing of the proposed action and reasons therefor, and afford the licensee or permittee at least thirty days to protest such proposed order of modification, except that where safety of life or property is involved the Commission may provide a shorter period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of proposed modification may be by notice of proposed rulemaking and email service
rubrics_metrics.description: The notification required may be effectuated by a notice of proposed rulemaking for modifications/additions to FM or television Table of Allotments or Table of Assignments. The Commission shall send a copy of any such NPRM to the affected licensee/permittee by email. For Wireless Radio Services, notification shall be by email and afford at least 30 days to protest (with safety exceptions and Federal Register timing exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of others to protest a proposed modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other licensee or permittee who believes that its license or permit would be modified by the proposed action may also protest the proposed action before its effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests subject to section 309 petition to deny requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any protest filed pursuant to this section shall be subject to the requirements of section 309 of the Communications Act, as amended, for petitions to deny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proceeding and proof in hearings on modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case where a hearing proceeding is conducted pursuant to this section, both the burden of proceeding with the introduction of evidence and the burden of proof shall be upon the Commission except that, with respect to any issue that pertains to whether the proposed action would modify the license or permit of a person filing a protest, such burdens shall be as described by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a written appearance to preserve right to hearing and present evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: To use the right to a hearing and the opportunity to give evidence upon the issues specified in any order designating a matter for hearing, any licensee or permittee, itself or by counsel, shall, within the period specified in that order, file with the Commission a written appearance stating that it will present evidence on the matters specified and, if required, appear before the presiding officer at a date/time to be determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of right to protest or hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to file a protest or the right to a hearing shall be deemed waived unless good cause is shown in a petition filed not later than 5 days before the lapse of time specified; waiver occurs upon failure to timely file protest or failure to file required written statement or failure to appear at hearing after filing a written statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If waived, licensee/permittee will be deemed to have consented to the modification as proposed and a final decision may be issued accordingly; Commission may still designate for hearing on its own motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of modification content and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Any order of modification issued pursuant to this section shall include a statement of the findings and the grounds and reasons therefor, shall specify the effective date of the modification, and shall be served on the licensee or permittee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predesignation pleading procedure for broadcast investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where an investigation is being conducted by the Commission in connection with the operation of a broadcast station or a pending renewal application, the licensee may file a written statement setting forth its views regarding the matters under investigation; the staff may, in its discretion, advise such licensee of the general nature of the investigation and of its opportunity to submit such a statement.
